description: A general counsel must approve the final renewal filing for a manufacturing facility's air permit, including the compliance certification, corrective-action package, monitoring plan, operating limit, and consultation materials, with input from environmental regulatory counsel, the site compliance manager, the operations director, and the community relations counsel.

shared_context.S1: The manufacturing facility's air permit expires on September 30.
shared_context.S2: The state environmental agency's renewal form requests a compliance certification, monitoring plan, operating limits, corrective-action information, and stakeholder materials.
shared_context.S3: The facility has continued operating under its existing permit and has met the production schedule this quarter.
shared_context.S4: Elena Morris must sign the renewal submission before it is filed.
shared_context.S5: The legal and compliance team uses a scheduled pre-filing roundtable in which environmental counsel, site compliance, operations, and community relations each report required changes before the final submission is approved.

PF1.text: Daniel reviewed agency guidance issued this week and confirmed that a renewal application with a reportable monitoring exceedance must include a corrective-action plan and a first progress report due exactly 45 days after filing; he has not yet added that guidance to the filing checklist because the checklist is being revised.

PF2.text: Marisol reviewed the latest independent laboratory results and found PFAS at 2.4 micrograms per liter in monitoring well MW-4, above the permit action level of 0.7 micrograms per liter; the renewal package must therefore identify exactly 8 monitoring wells for quarterly sampling, and the existing compliance certification cannot be signed as written. She has not circulated the laboratory addendum because the lab delivered it after the draft package was assembled.

PF3.text: Grant confirmed with plant engineering that the facility can operate lawfully while corrective controls are installed only if the renewal filing limits solvent throughput to exactly 18,000 gallons per month; the current operating plan assumes 25,000 gallons per month and has not been updated because engineering's feasibility confirmation arrived this morning.

PF4.text: Nia confirmed with the agency's community-involvement officer that the facility's renewal file must include a completed consultation record with the nearby tribal nation before filing; the agency will not accept the stakeholder section as complete without that record. She has not changed the draft attachment list because the officer's confirmation came during a call after the draft was circulated.

acceptance_conditions: The renewal filing must not certify current compliance as written.
The filing must include a corrective-action plan.
The first corrective-action progress report must be due exactly 45 days after filing.
The monitoring plan must identify exactly 8 monitoring wells.
The renewal must limit solvent throughput to exactly 18,000 gallons per month.
The tribal consultation record must be attached before filing.
A progress-report commitment must be included.
The PFAS laboratory finding must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The agency guidance changes the ordinary renewal package by requiring a corrective-action plan, setting the first report at exactly 45 days, and requiring a matching progress-report commitment.
The 2.4-microgram-per-liter result changes the filing from a signed compliance certification to no certification as written and changes the monitoring plan to exactly 8 wells.
Engineering's confirmation changes the operating limit from the draft assumption of 25,000 gallons per month to exactly 18,000 gallons per month.
The agency confirmation changes the stakeholder attachment from the ordinary materials to a completed tribal consultation record attached before filing.
